builder_plan.scenario: A workflow needs specialist review, but extra agents may add more cost than useful work.
builder_plan.change: Test the proposed division of work against a single-agent implementation.
builder_plan.baseline: One agent with the same tools and an equal total token and time budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted outputs, coordination failures, wall-clock time, and total cost across all agents.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Dynamic Task Allocation with Dialogue
summary: Replaces static or purely LLM-driven task allocation with a probabilistic framework that uses dialogue to reduce uncertainty in multi-agent coordination. Costs include maintaining explicit belief states, implementing structured communication protocols, and added decision and coordination overhead. It can fail if belief models are misspecified, dialogue is unreliable or misinterpreted, or the environment is too dynamic for the Bayesian updates to remain accurate.
rationale: The framework shows measurable gains in partially observable multi-agent settings but requires implementation effort and validation on the reader’s specific workloads before adoption.

claims.statement: Replaces static or purely LLM-driven task allocation with a probabilistic framework that uses dialogue to reduce uncertainty in multi-agent coordination. Costs include maintaining explicit belief states, implementing structured communication protocols, and added decision and coordination overhead. It can fail if belief models are misspecified, dialogue is unreliable or misinterpreted, or the environment is too dynamic for the Bayesian updates to remain accurate.
Under partial observability, the agent achieves an average speedup of 0.585 and completes tasks on average 18 timesteps faster than a non-communicating baseline as complexity increases.
